alternatives.labelRationale: The route retains a substantial biomedical and behavioural core while adding programming, data science, machine learning, medical imaging, robotics and AI ethics. The label states this interdisciplinary direction without claiming a dedicated clinical-technology qualification.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route removes dedicated epidemiology, anatomy, molecular cell biology, biochemistry, infection and immunity, neurobiology, abnormal psychology, medical and health psychology, sociology, psychodiagnostics and lifespan psychology. It adds programming, mathematical methods, introductory and advanced data science, machine learning, computer vision, databases, algorithms, linear algebra, robotics and AI ethics. Thirteen courses are shared and eleven differ, shifting the organising logic from broad biomedical and behavioural study to computation and emerging healthcare technology.

alternatives.concept: Study what shapes health across populations. Combine epidemiology, health psychology and research methods with public economics, environmental justice and communication.

alternatives.labelRationale: The route centres epidemiology, prevention, biopsychosocial health, research, ethics, economics, organisational leadership, sociology, environmental governance and public communication. The label accurately describes an interdisciplinary public-health direction without claiming a professional public-health or healthcare qualification.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route removes the anatomy, cell biology, physiology, biochemistry, laboratory, pathology, immunology, mechanisms-of-disease, pharmacology, neurobiology, cognitive-neuroscience and psychodiagnostics sequence. It adds ethics, qualitative research, public and behavioural economics, organisational and diversity leadership, modern and contemporary sociology, sustainability governance, international-relations theory and persuasive communication. Eleven courses are shared with the closest match and six with the technology route. Its organising logic is prevention, populations, institutions and policy rather than biomedical mechanisms or technology development.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme’s integrated health-and-disease, cross-disciplinary and care-and-society interests. Two further coherent directions remain. Explicit interests in technology, future healthcare and ethical challenges support a health-technology, data and AI route; explicit interests in prevention, epidemics, greener healthcare, living environments and population health support a public-health, policy and society route. All three schedules are feasible and substantively distinct: the closest and technology routes share 13 courses, the closest and public-health routes share 11, and the technology and public-health routes share 6. The maximum of three alternatives is therefore reached.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both study normal physiological regulation, including homeostasis. Utrecht also examines disruptions to that balance.
Both study anatomy and organ systems. Utrecht compares development and structure across species.
Both study drug action, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Utrecht considers treatment across patient groups.
Both address microbes and infectious disease. UCR also develops the mechanisms of immune defence.
Both examine organ-system disease. Utrecht applies clinical reasoning to human and animal cases.
Both examine cells, signalling and molecular processes. Utrecht applies these to human and animal health.
Both examine ageing and later life. UCR focuses on psychological development across the lifespan.
Both examine mental health and behaviour. Utrecht integrates medical, pharmaceutical and veterinary perspectives.
Both use data and statistical inference to investigate empirical questions. The applications and software differ.
Utrecht studies early human and animal development in a dedicated course.

notes.text: Utrecht combines medicine, pharmacy and veterinary perspectives with placements and a final project. The UCR options explore related biomedical, behavioural, population-health and technology questions through Liberal Arts and Sciences.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Dutch-taught Clinical Sciences degree, Zorg, gezondheid en samenleving, connects medicine, pharmacy and veterinary science with questions about health and society.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR examples focus on health and disease, health technology and data, or public health and policy.

cellNotes.text: Both study normal physiological regulation, including homeostasis. Utrecht also examines disruptions to that balance.
Both study anatomy and organ systems. Utrecht compares development and structure across species.
Both study drug action, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Utrecht considers treatment across patient groups.
Both address microbes and infectious disease. UCR also develops the mechanisms of immune defence.
Both examine organ-system disease. Utrecht applies clinical reasoning to human and animal cases.
Both examine cells, signalling and molecular processes. Utrecht applies these to human and animal health.
Both examine ageing and later life. UCR focuses on psychological development across the lifespan.
Both examine mental health and behaviour. Utrecht integrates medical, pharmaceutical and veterinary perspectives.
Both use data and statistical inference to investigate empirical questions. The applications and software differ.
